verses.1: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Until my death, you will continue to mourn for Saul. But I will appoint a king over Israel from your descendants. He will have your lineage. Go and send him to Gibeah of Saul, so that I may see in his descendants a king for me.”
verses.2: And Shemuel said, “How can I go?” Then Shaul heard this and killed him. Shemuel said, “The oxen for the sacrifice must be taken in your hands.” You said that you would offer them as sacrifices to Jehovah.
verses.3: And you called for Ishmael at the sacrifice. And I will tell you what you must do, and what you must eat in accordance with what I have commanded you.
verses.4: And Shemuel did what the LORD said. He went into the storeroom where the bread was kept. The elders of the city were afraid when they heard his voice. They said, “Shalom! Come in.”
verses.5: And Shalom said to the priests, “Let us go and offer sacrifices to Yahweh. I will become holy, and you also come with me to offer sacrifices.” Then he sanctified His own son and his sons, and called them together for the sacrifice.
verses.6: And when they came in, they saw Eliezer. They said, “But here is the Messiah, who stands against Jehovah.”
verses.7: And the LORD said to Shemaiah, “Do not look at his appearance or at his height. For he will be despised by people, because man sees only with his eyes, but the LORD sees with his heart.”
verses.8: And Ishai called Abinadav, and he brought him before Shemuel. And Shemuel said, “Also, do not choose Jehovah.”
verses.9: And Yishai Samah said, “Also in this case, Jehovah did not choose.”
verses.10: And Ishmael passed his seven sons before Samuel. Then Samuel said to Ishmael, “The LORD has not chosen these.”
verses.11: And Shemuel said to Jesse, “Let the boys go.” Then he said, “The little one still has time. Look at him; he’s already ready.” Shemuel said to Jesse, “Send him away, for we won’t wait until he comes here.”
verses.12: And He sent for him, and brought him back. He was a man with beautiful eyes and good looks. And Jehovah said, “Let us destroy him, for he is such a person.”
verses.13: And Shemuel took the staff of God, and he used it to strike his brothers. From that day on, the wind of God blew upon David. Then Shemuel stood up and went away.
verses.14: And the Spirit of Jehovah departed from Shaul. At that time, a wicked spirit came from Jehovah.
verses.15: And the servants of Shaul said to him, “Please, let the spirit of God descend upon you.”
verses.16: Please say, “Our Lord, your servants stand before you. Let someone who knows how to play the instrument play it for you. May God’s spirit be upon you, and may it be played by someone who truly understands how to play it. Then it will be good for you.”
verses.17: And Shaul said to his servants, “Please see for me who is able to play the instrument. Bring him to me.”
verses.18: And one of the boys said, “Look! I saw a boy from the house of Lachmi. He knows how to play music and is a great warrior. He’s also very intelligent and knows many things. May Jehovah be with him.”
verses.19: And Shaul sent demons to Isai. He said, “Send me your son David from Bethlehem.”
verses.20: And Ishai took some bread, some oil, and a few goats’ cheeses. He sent them to David’s son, to Shaul.
verses.21: And David went before Shaul. He stood before him and loved him greatly. And he became his favorite companion.
verses.22: And Shaul sent someone to Ishai, saying, “Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.”
verses.23: And when the spirit of God came upon Shaul, David took the censer and burned incense before it. Then the spirit of God was good to Shaul, and evil spirits departed from him.
